normalization.overview: Levent Alpöge claims a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis and Dirichlet GRH, with substantial independent Lean verification reported by MIT.
normalization.whyItMatters: A formal kernel accepting precisely stated theorems is substantially stronger evidence than an AI-generated argument, but does not settle discovery attribution or community comprehension.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Track immutable proof artifacts, exact mathematical targets, independent checker results, limits and acceptance decisions separately. Verification is not a headline.
normalization.falsification: Review kernel or comparator rejection, nonstandard axioms, statement mismatch, faulty dependencies, a changed source archive, or a documented flaw in interpretation; publish timestamped revisions, not silent assertions.
normalization.freshness: MIT independent verification as of 2026-11-21 12:55 UTC. All technical results are MIT-reported and not re-executed by GhostMesh. End-to-end Lean checks remain running.

claims.proposition: Alpöge and Claude developed a complete proof of classical RH and Dirichlet GRH.
claims.assessment: The original author claims this. MIT independently reports a complete machine-readable formalization and multiple successful checks.
claims.limits: The main end-to-end lake comparator and Lean full-export replays remain running. Human comprehension and broad community acceptance are separate.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: The published Lean submission compiles 175,187 modules and depends only on standard Lean axioms.
claims.assessment: MIT reports successful compilation of all modules, zero errors, only three standard axioms and independent module replay.
claims.limits: The report is third-party verified but not reproduced by GhostMesh. The build was unsandboxed and not a complete byte-for-byte lake build.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: Independent nanoda and con-leche kernels accept the full exported proof.
claims.assessment: MIT reports acceptance by two separate kernel implementations and comparison of the five statements against the independent challenge.
claims.limits: This is independent checker implementation, not separate mathematical research-team replication or comprehensive human audit.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: The classical RH theorem targets Mathlib native RiemannHypothesis, while scoped GRH concerns Dirichlet L-functions.
claims.assessment: The source inspection reports Mathlib statement and five challenge comparisons with explicit Dirichlet scope.
claims.limits: Extended RH, Dedekind zeta and Hecke L-functions are outside the verified claim.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: The submitted classical RH proof implies Robin and Lagarias inequalities when combined with Robin1984.
claims.assessment: MIT reports successful combined compilation, standard-axiom audit and independent nanoda/con-leche acceptance of both divisor-sum theorems.
claims.limits: This is an arithmetic cross-check using a separate formalization, not an independent new proof; combined lake comparator still running.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: Claude made the decisive creative steps in Alpöge’s discovery.
claims.assessment: The original author credits Claude for significant technical moves.
claims.limits: Formal proof objects do not establish who first proposed individual ideas or provide a session-by-session verified provenance.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.

claims.proposition: The mathematical community or Clay has officially accepted a solved Riemann Hypothesis.
claims.assessment: Neither institutional acceptance nor prize decision has been established; Clay still lists RH as unsolved.
claims.limits: Institutional status is not a counterexample to a formally verified proposition.
claims.temporalScope: As of the time-stamped November 21 verification update; a later check may change status.
